title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 80-82). On the previous page Grothendieck starts from a ⊗-additive category P_1 where homogeneous polynomial maps of degree p are represented by divided powers Γ^p. He extracts four pieces of structure:
- a functor Γ^*: P_1 → graded objects that turns ⊕ into ⊗;
- hence a graded commutative ⊗-algebra structure on each Γ^*(X);
- natural maps α^X_{p,q}: Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)), modelled on x^{[pq]} ↦ (x^{[q]})^{[p]};
- an associativity square for α (labelled (**) on p. 80) and unit isomorphisms Γ^1 = id, Γ^0 = 1.

This page states the converse axiomatics ('Inversement'). Let P_1 be a ⊗-additive (symmetric monoidal additive) category equipped with a functor Γ^*: (P_1,⊕) → (graded objects of P_1, ⊗) with the following properties:
- It is a ⊗-functor: Γ^*(0) = 1, i.e. Γ^0(0) = 1 and Γ^i(0) = 0 for i ≠ 0.
- Γ^*(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ^*(X)⊗Γ^*(Y) as graded rings, functorially in X and Y, compatibly with the unit, associativity and commutativity constraints.
- It is normalized: Γ^i = 0 for i < 0, Γ^0 = 1, Γ^1 = id.
- It carries natural transformations α_{p,q}: Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q satisfying the associativity square of p. 80.
- It satisfies unit axioms: α_{1,q} = id and α_{q,1} = id (using Γ^1 = id); α_{0,q} = id: Γ^0 → Γ^0Γ^q = Γ^0; and α_{q,0}: Γ^0 = 1 → Γ^q(1).

In modern terms this is the following package:
- a symmetric-monoidal 'exponential' functor (Seely-type isomorphism Γ(X⊕Y) ≅ ΓX⊗ΓY);
- which is also a comonad graded by the multiplicative monoid (N,×): counit/dereliction Γ^1 = id, comultiplication/digging Γ^{pq} → Γ^pΓ^q, with coassociativity and counit laws;
- with Γ^0 = 1 handling degree 0.

The purpose shows on the next page. One defines P_p(X,Y) := Hom(Γ^p X, Y), the 'homogeneous polynomial maps of degree p'. Composition P_p(X,Y) × P_q(Y,Z) → P_{pq}(X,Z) is g∘f = g·Γ^q(f)·α_{q,p}. This is exactly the graded co-Kleisli category of the graded comonad. The page thus recovers, from Γ-data alone, a category of polynomial maps graded by (N,×), in which P_1 is the linear category itself.

In the dossier this serves the 'structures multiplicatives' on ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes: extending divided-power and power operations (à la Dold–Puppe) to complexes needs an intrinsic axiomatization of 'maps of degree p'.
errors: α_{q,0}: 1 → Γ^q(1) is marked 'unique', which is unjustified: Hom(1, Γ^q(1)) is not a singleton in general. It must be imposed as a datum or axiom (the element γ_q(1) = 1). Grothendieck notices this himself on the next page ('Je l'avais oublié dans les axiomes préliminaires').

Compatibility of α_{p,q} with the exponential (graded ring) isomorphism Γ^*(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ^*X⊗Γ^*Y is not stated. In divided-power algebras, γ_p(γ_q(x+y)) has to interact with the multiplicative structure, so additional coherence is needed for the converse to recover a genuine divided-power/polynomial structure.
Minor notation: the transformation is written α_M instead of α_{p,q}, and the label (**) is reused, though it already denoted associativity on p. 80.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of divided powers on a ⊗-additive category: an exponential functor Γ^*: (P,⊕) → (Grad P,⊗) with Γ^0 = 1, Γ^1 = id, plus natural maps Γ^{pq} → Γ^pΓ^q satisfying associativity and unit laws
ideas.modern_name: Comonad graded by the monoid (N,×) that is also strong symmetric monoidal from (⊕) to (⊗); 'graded exponential modality' (Seely isomorphism + digging/dereliction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Graded exponentials: Girard–Scedrov–Scott (Bounded Linear Logic, 1992); graded comonads/monads: Brunel–Gaboardi–Mazza–Zdancewic, Katsumata (2014); divided powers as polynomial-law representers: Roby (1963)

ideas.what: Plethysm-type map Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)), x^{[pq]} ↦ (x^{[q]})^{[p]}, with associativity
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power composition / comultiplication of the graded comonad Γ (dual to the multiplication Sym^p Sym^q → Sym^{pq})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical divided-power axioms (Cartan, Roby); plethysm in strict polynomial functors (Friedlander–Suslin 1997, Touzé)
ideas.where_published: Divided powers in crystalline cohomology context via Berthelot; not this axiomatic form

ideas.what: Recovering a category of homogeneous polynomial maps P_p(X,Y) = Hom(Γ^p X, Y), with composition of degree pq, from the Γ-data (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Graded co-Kleisli category of a graded comonad; category of homogeneous polynomial laws
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws); graded co-Kleisli: programming-semantics literature (2010s)

missed.claim: The page anticipates the structure later isolated in bounded/graded linear logic: an exponential Γ with a Seely isomorphism Γ(X⊕Y) ≅ ΓX⊗ΓY, dereliction Γ^1 = id, digging Γ^{pq} → Γ^pΓ^q indexed by the multiplicative monoid, and a co-Kleisli category of 'degree-p maps'. Grothendieck's motivating model is divided powers in module/perfect-complex categories, which coincides with the standard symmetric-tensor model of the exponential. No link between his divided-power axiomatics and graded exponential comonads appears in the literature.
missed.quote: supposons de plus donnés des homs de foncteurs Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q ... satisfaisant à la condition d'associativité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an algebro-geometric, characteristic-free (divided powers rather than symmetric powers) source for graded exponentials. It suggests that categories of strict polynomial maps and polynomial laws are graded co-Kleisli categories, which could inform both the semantics of quantitative/bounded linear logic and the formalism of strict polynomial functors and derived divided powers.

missed.claim: A converse characterization (a ⊗-additive category with such Γ-data is equivalent to a 'category with polynomial maps' graded by (N,×)) is begun but left incomplete. Missing are the axioms relating α to the exponential isomorphism and the datum 1 → Γ^q(1).
missed.quote: Inversement, soit P_1 ⊗ additive ... munie d'un ⊗ foncteur ... Γ^*:(P_1,⊕)→(P_1^{gr},⊗)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean equivalence between 'divided-power structures on additive symmetric monoidal (∞-)categories' and 'polynomial enrichments' is relevant to current work on derived divided powers and derived rings (Brantner–Mathew, Raksit), where such axiomatics are reconstructed from scratch.

deep.surprise_reason: The divided-power axioms themselves are classical. Notable is the structural packaging: an exponential functor that is also an (N,×)-graded comonad, with a graded co-Kleisli category of polynomial maps. This matches later graded-exponential and graded-comonad notions from logic, and that link to Grothendieck is not recorded. It is, however, an incomplete sketch, and partial analogues (Roby, strict polynomial functors) exist.
transcription_corrections: '⊗ additive avec √' : the '√' is most likely an insertion caret for the interlinear 'avec' / 'ou addition', not a square-root symbol.
'(P_{1+}^{gr.d.},⊗)' should read '(P_1^{grad.},⊗)', i.e. graded objects of P_1.
'Γ^{pq} →^{α_M} Γ^p∘Γ^q' : the label is read as α_M in the image, but mathematically it is α_{p,q}, and α_M^X stands for α^X_{p,q}.
'(fonct. en foncteurs en M)' may read '(iso de foncteurs en M)'.
The second unit display is labelled '(***)' in the image; the first is '(**)' or '(*.*)' — distinct from the associativity (**) of p. 80.
